title: lore agents renders Constitution core and Constants pointer into the managed block (OPAG-425 R8)
description: Binding record: opum-doc main 7831fff, docs/adr/add-constitution-and-constants-document-types-to-lore.md, R8. When a Constitution exists, lore agents renders a short core into its managed block: path, version, and each principle id with its MUST/MUST NOT lines, nothing more. When a Constants document exists, one pointer line with an observable trigger (e.g. 'before writing or changing a name, identifier, prefix, URL or pinned value, read <path>'), plus 'id = value' for entries flagged hot. lore agents --check reports drift when either document changes (the OPAG-378 managed-block carve-out already covers lore agents). lore init's default .lore/agents profiles pin the Constitution. Depends on the two type tasks.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore agents renders exactly path, version and principle ids with MUST/MUST NOT lines for a Constitution, and the trigger line plus hot id = value lines for Constants, proven by tests
lore agents --check reports drift after either document changes
lore init default agent profiles pin the Constitution

implementationNotes: DESIGN (branch feat/LCLI-597-agents-render-constitution). New optional TypeRule facet agentBlock in core/type-rules.ts, registered for Constitution and Constants, plus agentBlockLines(docs), which renders in registry order and names no type, the same pattern as check/seed/bundle. The Constitution render reuses findSection and a new splitPrinciples, now shared with principleFindings, and paragraphLines, which gains a render object: probe text decides whether a line is MUST/MUST NOT and display text renders it. It emits path, version, and each P<n> heading with its MUST lines. Rationale: and Check: lines are excluded even when they say MUST, and a MUST inside a code span does not count. The Constants render reuses parseConstants and emits the ADR R8 trigger verbatim ('before writing or changing a name, identifier, prefix, URL or pinned value, read <path>'), then id = value for hot:true entries that are status active with a well-formed id, first occurrence only. Deprecated and retired hot entries are left out (Amendment 2; R6 warns on citing either). This narrows R8's literal 'entries flagged hot' and is flagged for the orchestrator. Sanitising: prose has backslash and < escaped, so no raw HTML or marker can enter the block, then passes through agent-plugins printable() (stripAnsiAndControls composed with a whitespace collapse). Literals go into code spans fenced longer than any backtick run. errors.ts is untouched. Hook: commands/agent-governance.ts readAgentGovernance(root) walks docs/ and resolves types exactly as check's per-file peek does (loadProfile, profileForBundle over loadBundleState, effectiveProfileFor, canonicalType, typeRuleFor), so R12 holds. The first document per type in sorted order wins, and a file with unparseable frontmatter is skipped. It is called in applyAgentsBridge (lore agents and lore init --claude) and applyCodexBridge (lore init --codex) and passed to both nudge builders through withGovernance(). With no lines, the body is returned unchanged.

EVIDENCE. test/agents-governance.test.ts has 21 cases, all passing. AC1: exact lines for the Constitution fixture and the Constants fixture; absence of rationale, Check:, SHOULD, MAY, prose, preamble and governance; absence of non-hot, hot:false, deprecated and retired entries; exact CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md blocks. AC2: separate Constitution-drift and Constants-drift cases, each with an unchanged-document positive control (exit 0, unchanged) followed by an edit (exit 6, updated), plus Codex drift and init --claude. Absent documents: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md blocks equal LITERAL pre-R8 text, with only the topic list interpolated. MUTATIONS, predicted in the test header before running. (1) Renderer also emits Rationale: lines: exactly the 9 of 21 named went red, 12 green. (2) Discovery ignores Constants: exactly 1 of 21 red ('Constants drift'). Its containment assertion fired first, so I re-ran with that assertion disabled and the drift assertion itself failed (expected 6, received 0). Both mutations reverted and grep-confirmed. GATES (lore 0.9.3 from source, quest 0.10.0): bun test 3753 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail across 113 files; bun run lore check 82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0; bun run typecheck exit 0; bunx biome check on changed files exit 0 with 1 warning on a pre-existing origin/dev line (agents.ts hasCodexBridge). This repo (no Constitution or Constants): bun run src/cli.ts agents --check reports both files unchanged, exit 0, before and after the change; the walk read 82 markdown files and rendered 0 lines.

AC3 NOT DONE, premise absent. lore init creates no .lore/agents profiles anywhere in src/. The only .lore/agents code is AGENT_PROFILES_DIR in core/agent-profile.ts; scaffold.ts and init.ts write config.toml and profile.toml only, and this repo's three profiles are hand-written. A pinned reference must resolve against the bundle (specs/agent-profile-context-retrieval), so a default profile pinning a Constitution a fresh init does not have would make lore check fail. Satisfying AC3 means new init output (an external contract), which makes it a design question for opum-agent. Options: (A) lore init writes default profiles, pinning the Constitution only when one exists; (B) lore agent context implicitly pins the bundle's Constitution for every profile. Left unchecked rather than satisfied on a weaker reading.

REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (second commit on the branch). Rulings: opum-agent 2026-09-26T22:00:21Z; opum-doc Constitution/Constants Amendment 4 pending. (1) AC3 goes to option B: lore agent context auto-pins the Constitution, in a follow-up task the parent files; not built here, AC3 stays unchecked. (2) Active-only hot entries confirmed. (3) The full 'P1. <Name>' heading, listed even with no MUST rule, confirmed. (4) Failing loud on a malformed profile.toml or docs/index.md confirmed. FIXES. B1 (blocking): rules are judged and rendered per PARAGRAPH (the new paragraphTexts, which paragraphLines is now built on), with soft and hard breaks joined by a space. A paragraph's rule ends at the first line opening a Rationale: or Check: label, bold or not, so a paragraph that opens with a label contributes nothing, and a label line with no blank line before it still ends the rule. S1: escapeProse backslash-escapes every ASCII punctuation character (the full CommonMark-escapable set) after stripping ANSI and control bytes per line. It strips first because escaping [ would split an ESC [31m sequence into pieces the strip no longer recognises. Line endings are kept so display lines stay aligned with probe lines for the label cut. The validated P<n>. prefix is emitted verbatim and only the name is escaped. The false 'cannot open raw HTML' claims in type-rules.ts, cli-surface.md and instructions.ts are corrected. Cost: the raw block shows backslashes (input\.). S2: discovery uses the new commands/discover.ts walkUnignoredMarkdown plus gitIgnoredEntries, the same ignored-files query as check.ts's private copy. check.ts is owned by other work, so it is not yet switched over: FOLLOW-UP, point check.ts's expandRoot at the shared helper. S3: ANSI/control tests added for a principle heading and for a rule. S5: readSource is now inside the skip, and bundle state is resolved in agent-governance.ts so every error names docs/index.md. NIT: agentCode turns <!-- and --> into entities; inside a code span an entity shows as written, so a value holding either displays <!-- / -->. Not done here: S4 bidi (LCLI-607 #307), the rollout note (LCLI-599), errors.ts, CHANGELOG.md.

NARROWED ESCAPE and DEV MERGE (third commit on the branch, after merging origin/dev 53d8912d, #307). Per the coordinator: agents read the raw CLAUDE.md, so escaping ordinary punctuation was noise in always-loaded context. escapeProse now strips first (ANSI, control bytes, and since #307 bidi and invisible format characters), then escapes only INLINE_SIGNIFICANT anywhere: backslash, backtick, *, _, [, ], <, >, &, !, |, ~. The new escapeItemStart escapes a leading #, -, +, = and the delimiter of a leading ordered-list marker (1. becomes 1\.), applied where a rule starts its nested list item. . , - ( ) : and the rest stay literal mid-text. The heading name is never at an item start (it follows P<n>.), so it gets only the inline set. MEASURED, not assumed: a probe rendered 512 rules through agentBlockLines, every ASCII punctuation character at start, mid-word, spaced, repeated and around parens and brackets, and parsed each back with mdast-util-from-markdown (CommonMark, the only parser in the repo): no live node. Positive control on the same detector: the unescaped variants are live for 8 characters (# * + - > _ backtick ~). So no unexpected mid-text character is live under CommonMark, and nothing extra is escaped. Caveat: GitHub's GFM would still autolink a bare URL or email mid-text; that shows the author's own text, and the repo has no GFM parser to measure it. S4 closes by inheritance: a U+202E rule test passes via #307's strip. TESTS: 51 in test/agents-governance.test.ts. All 9 S1 class cases are unchanged and pass. Added: a readability case (the coordinator's force-push rule renders byte-identical, no backslash anywhere), a mid-text-literal case, five line-start cases (+, =, ---, 1., 12)) and the bidi case. MUTATIONS, predicted in the test header before running: & dropped gave exactly 1 of 51 red (entity); line-start # dropped gave exactly 1 (heading); strip removed gave exactly 3 (two ANSI, one bidi); Constants discovery ignored gave exactly 1. B1 revert: my first mutant bypassed mustRule, which now also carries escapeItemStart, and turned 10 red: the 3 B1 cases plus the 7 line-start cases (heading, list item, +, =, ---, 1., 12)). That mutant removed two fixes, not one. Rebuilt to revert only B1 (escapeItemStart kept per line), it turned exactly 3 red. All reverted, no marker left.
